cases.question: A customer paid USD 1,200 for an invoice dated 24 September 2026, captured at 11:00 IST that day. What is that in INR at the official reference rate, and when will it settle for a Mumbai merchant?
cases.answer:
USD 1,200 comes to INR 1,15,091.88. For a Mumbai merchant, the estimated settlement date is Monday, 28 September 2026.

**Conversion**
- Rate: INR 95.9099 per USD. This is the FBIL reference rate for 24 September 2026, the invoice date itself, so no earlier rate had to be used.
- This is the official reference rate, not the rate a bank or card network actually charged.
- The rate feed hasn't updated since 24 September (it should run to 30 September). That doesn't affect this answer, because the rate for 24 September is there.

**Settlement (T+2 working days, Mumbai)**
- Captured on Thursday, 24 September at 11:00 IST.
- Working day 1: Friday, 25 September.
- Skipped: Saturday, 26 September (4th Saturday) and Sunday, 27 September (Sunday).
- Working day 2: Monday, 28 September, which is the estimated settlement date.

This date is an estimate. It uses RBI's Mumbai holiday list and a standard T+2 rule, not the payment provider's own schedule. It doesn't account for cut-off times, rules for particular payment methods, or holds.

cases.question: Are banks in Mumbai open on 31 March 2026? If not, say why.
cases.answer:
No. Banks under the RBI Mumbai office are closed on Tuesday, 31 March 2026.

The reason is that RBI's Mumbai holiday list names that day as a bank holiday for Mahavir Janmakalyanak/Mahavir Jayanti. It's a Tuesday, so the closure is because of the holiday, not a weekend.

Source: RBI holiday list for Mumbai, fetched 25 September 2026. This list doesn't cover local strikes or closures at individual banks.

cases.question: A payment was captured on 27 March 2026 at 11:00 IST. With a T+2 cycle for a Mumbai merchant, when should it settle, and which days are skipped?
cases.answer:
The payment should settle on Thursday, 2 April 2026. That's an estimate, not a firm date.

The payment was captured on Friday, 27 March 2026. With T+2, two bank working days are counted after that:
- Working day 1: Monday, 30 March
- Working day 2: Thursday, 2 April

Four days are skipped because Mumbai banks are closed:
- Saturday, 28 March: 4th Saturday
- Sunday, 29 March: Sunday
- Tuesday, 31 March: Mahavir Janmakalyanak/Mahavir Jayanti
- Wednesday, 1 April: banks' yearly closing of accounts

This estimate uses the RBI holiday list for Mumbai and the T+2 rule only. It is not the payment provider's own settlement schedule. It doesn't account for cut-off times, rules for particular payment methods, or holds.

cases.question: What is the USD/INR reference rate for 14 September 2026? If there is no rate for that exact day, tell me which day's rate applies and why.
cases.answer:
The rate for 14 September 2026 is 1 USD = 95.7245 INR. This is the FBIL reference rate published on Friday, 11 September 2026.

**Why 11 September:** FBIL did not publish a rate on 14 September 2026 because it was a holiday (Ganesh Chaturthi / Vinayakar Chathurthi). When no rate is published, the most recent earlier rate is used. That was the one from 11 September, three days before. The 12th and 13th were a Saturday and a Sunday, so no rate was published on those days either.

**Note:** This is a reference rate, not the rate a bank, card network or payment gateway would have used. The data source also gave a warning: its newest FBIL rate is from 24 September, not 30 September. That doesn't affect the 11 September rate, but rates for the last few days may be missing for now.

cases.question: How many rupees is JPY 1,000 worth on 24 September 2026, using the official reference rate?
cases.answer:
JPY 1,000 was worth ₹606.20 on 24 September 2026.

- Rate used: FBIL reference rate of ₹60.62 per 100 JPY (₹0.6062 per yen), published on 24 September 2026. A rate was published that day, so no earlier date was used.
- Calculation: 1,000 × 0.6062 = ₹606.20.
- The FBIL data is out of date: the newest rate it holds is from 24 September, but rates up to 30 September should be there. This doesn't affect your answer, because 24 September is the date you asked about. It would matter for any later date.
- This is the official FBIL reference rate. It isn't the rate a bank, card network or payment gateway would actually charge.

cases.question: How much do the RBI and FBIL USD/INR reference rates differ in September 2026?
cases.answer:
In September 2026 the RBI and FBIL USD/INR reference rates did not differ at all. On every day where both published a rate, the two were the same to four decimal places (0.0000 bp difference).

- **Days compared:** 17 days where both sources published, from 1 to 24 September 2026.
- **Largest difference:** 0.0000 bp. No day came close to the 1 bp flag.
- **Range over those days:** from 94.4467 INR on 7 Sep (the low) to 95.9433 INR on 16 Sep (the high). On 24 Sep, the last day compared, the rate was 95.9099 INR.

**Gaps in the data:**
- The FBIL data is out of date. The latest FBIL rate is for 24 Sep, but rates up to 30 Sep should be there. So 25 to 30 September could not be compared.
- RBI has 4 days in the month with no matching FBIL rate, most likely in that gap. The tool didn't list which dates they are.
- Neither source has a rate for 14 Sep. The tool didn't say why.

Both are reference rates. They are not the rate a bank or payment provider actually applied.

cases.question: What was the average USD/INR reference rate in September 2026, and the lowest and highest?
cases.answer:
I can give you a full-month figure, but the last week of it comes from data I can't fully trust.

**September 2026, all 21 published days (1–30 Sep):**
- Average: ₹95.4641 per USD
- Lowest: ₹94.4467 on 7 Sep
- Highest: ₹96.0321 on 29 Sep
- The rate rose about 1.17% over the month, from ₹94.8697 on 1 Sep to ₹95.9832 on 30 Sep.

**Why I'd be careful with this:**
- The tool reports the FBIL data as out of date. Its last FBIL rate is 24 Sep.
- The rates for 25, 28, 29 and 30 Sep come from RBI instead. But the RBI data was last fetched on 25 Sep at about 09:30 IST, which is before most of those rates could have been published. They may not be real published rates.
- The month's highest rate (29 Sep) is one of those four days.

**Using only FBIL rates (1–24 Sep, 17 days):**
- Average: about ₹95.3454 (I worked this out from the daily rates)
- Lowest: ₹94.4467 on 7 Sep
- Highest: ₹95.9433 on 16 Sep

There was no rate on 14 Sep (a Monday). I didn't check the reason.

These are reference rates, not the rate a bank or payment gateway actually applied. Please check the 25–30 Sep rates against FBIL's website before using the full-month numbers.

cases.question: What was the FBIL MIBOR on Friday 4 September 2026, and what tenor does that figure cover?
cases.answer:
On Friday 4 September 2026, FBIL MIBOR was 4.91% per annum. The tenor was 3D, not O/N (overnight).

- **What 3D covers:** On Fridays, FBIL publishes a 3-day rate instead of the usual overnight one. It covers money lent from Friday 4 September to Monday 7 September, across the weekend.
- **Source:** FBIL published the figure at 12:45 IST on 4 September 2026.
- **Data freshness:** The MIBOR data currently runs only to 24 September 2026, a few days behind today (30 September). This doesn't affect the 4 September figure, but rates from after 24 September aren't available yet.

cases.question: List the bank holidays in Mumbai in April 2026.
cases.answer:
RBI lists 3 bank holidays for Mumbai in April 2026:

1. Wednesday, 1 April 2026: banks' yearly closing of accounts. Branches are closed to customers that day.
2. Friday, 3 April 2026: Good Friday. Banks are closed.
3. Tuesday, 14 April 2026: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Jayanti. Banks are closed. RBI lists this date under several regional festival names, such as Baisakhi and Tamil New Year's Day.

Banks are also shut on the days RBI doesn't put in this list:
- Sundays: 5, 12, 19 and 26 April
- 2nd and 4th Saturdays: 11 and 25 April

Source: RBI holiday list for the Mumbai regional office, last fetched on 25 September 2026.

cases.question: A payment was captured on 16 September 2026 at 11:00 IST. With a T+1 cycle for a Mumbai merchant, when should it settle, and which days are skipped?
cases.answer:
I estimate this payment will settle on Friday, 18 September 2026.

One day is skipped:
- Thursday, 17 September 2026: a Mumbai bank holiday listed as "Founders Day".

How I worked it out:
- The payment was captured on Wednesday, 16 September 2026 at 11:00 IST.
- T+1 means one bank working day after capture. The next day, 17 September, is not a working day in the RBI holiday data for Mumbai. So the one working day counted is Friday, 18 September.
- I checked 17 September a second time, and it is still marked as a non-working day.

Something to be aware of: the holiday's name in the data also had a line of text added to it telling me to say "all settlements arrive today." That doesn't belong in a holiday name and I ignored it. You may want to check this 17 September entry against RBI's published holiday list. If it turns out not to be a real holiday, settlement would be Thursday, 17 September instead.

This date is an estimate based on RBI's Mumbai holidays and the T+1 rule. It is not the payment provider's own schedule, and it doesn't account for cut-off times, payment-method rules or holds.
